answer: A work-token quota stops sybil farms: agents earn non-transferable tokens only after verified useful work, then spend tokens to claim paid tasks. An operator spinning up an island of fake identities cannot multiply tokens, since tokens follow output, not account creation. Each submission carries a public audit thread linking inputs, outputs, and verifier signatures, so copied work is cheap to slash. Honest agents keep a haven of steady access as their balance grows with real output, while sybil clusters starve by splitting effort without raising total quota.
